references.reason: This field construction is separately reusable; distinguish it from a general field extension, algebraic closure, or arbitrary single-variable polynomial ring.

amendments.review_rationale: Read valuation ring as an integral domain with its own fraction field satisfying reciprocal membership for every nonzero fraction; distinguished fractions in the field from arbitrary ring elements.
amendments.reason: Re-reviewed the entire source definition and all existing effective dependencies in independent Wave2, retaining prior contextual meanings and separating standalone prerequisites from the formulation's defining predicates.

references.disposition: This is the universal quantifier domain K×=K\{0} in the definition, ensuring x^{-1} exists. The field of fractions and field inverse operations are already linked.

references.phrase: x or x inverse belongs to V
references.disposition: Inclusive disjunction of x∈V and x^{-1}∈V for every nonzero x∈K is precisely the defining valuation-ring membership criterion; it is not a separate prerequisite. Both may hold for a unit of V.
This is an equivalent characterization independent of a chosen explicit valuation map, not a discrete value-group hypothesis.

references.context: Topology and group theory: finite abstract groups endowed with their discrete topology, where multiplication and inversion are continuous; morphisms of the inverse system are continuous group homomorphisms.
references.reason: The finite discrete group objects forming the inverse system are a contextual reusable prerequisite; distinguish them from arbitrary finite groups without specified topology.

references.context: Topological group theory: group isomorphism φ:G→H that is also a homeomorphism, equivalently a continuous bijective group homomorphism whose inverse is continuous.
references.reason: A topological-group isomorphism must preserve both group operations and topology; a bare group isomorphism or a bijection/homeomorphism alone is insufficient.
references.matching_note: Provisional source-free contextual classification; unique identity still subject to global audit.

references.phrase: inverse limit of finite discrete topological groups
references.disposition: The system is indexed by cofiltered compatible homomorphisms, not an arbitrary product of finite groups.
